purpose: Teach: スタンプ/コロッケ/たこ焼き/シロ/タケ/カブ/みそ/ルータ

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、駅のスタンプラリー、流行っていた。
lines.en: When I was young, station stamp rallies were all the rage.
lines.style: Gentle opening, settling into memory. Slow, measured pace. Warm nostalgic tone with a soft smile in the voice. Let the image land before moving on.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。お肉屋さん、コロッケ、毎週買ったわね。
lines.en: Yes. We'd go to the butcher every week and buy croquettes.
lines.style: Bright affirmation, then tender descent into the specific memory. Soft, almost humming quality. Slight lingering on the croquettes — the taste memory is still there.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 夜店のたこ焼き、お祭りの思い出だ。
lines.en: Takoyaki at the festival stalls — those are the memories I hold onto.
lines.style: Quieter, more inward. Careful articulation on the festival name. Trailing off gently on the last phrase, as if touching something fragile.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 裏庭にいたシロ、いい犬だったわね。
lines.en: That white dog in our backyard, Shiro — he was a good dog.
lines.style: Slight catch in the voice on the dog's name, then immediate tenderness. Slower pace. Soft finality on the last phrase, like settling a memory into place.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 家の庭、タケが、自由に育ってる。
lines.en: The bamboo in our garden just grew wild and free.
lines.style: Lighter, almost wondering tone. Unhurried. A small smile audible. Let the image sit — not resigned, but accepting of growth beyond control.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お母さんの教えで、カブの漬物、覚えたわ。
lines.en: I learned to make turnip pickles from my mother's teaching.
lines.style: Soft, almost meditative. Careful on the word 'mother' — respect and affection both present. Slow hands in the voice. Trailing into a small, satisfied breath.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 家のみそ、毎年仕込んだなあ。
lines.en: Every year we'd make the house miso from scratch.
lines.style: Quieter nostalgia, almost to himself. Soft, rhythmic cadence — like the annual ritual itself. Wistful exhale on 'every year,' trailing off with the weight of repetition and care.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 孫が、ルータ、設定し直してくれた。
lines.en: My grandchild came and set up the router for us.
lines.style: Warm and present — the shift is palpable. Lighter touch, almost amused at the contrast. Gentle pride on 'grandchild,' then a soft, satisfied close. The future meeting the past.
